page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.32xlarge is an enterprise-scale virtual instance positioned within the general-purpose compute category. Operating under the KVM hypervisor on x86_64 architecture, it is powered by AMD EPYC 7H12 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. It operates without hardware GPU accelerators.

Storage architecture on the ecs.g6a.32xlarge relies entirely on network-attached block devices, as no local NVMe or SSD storage is bundled with the instance. For inter-system communication and remote disk access, the instance is equipped with a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. This network speed provides the throughput necessary to sustain high volumes of concurrent client connections and substantial storage traffic without relying on on-box ephemeral disks.

By consolidating 128 dedicated AMD cores and half a terabyte of memory into a single instance, the ecs.g6a.32xlarge offers significant hardware density for horizontally scaled or highly threaded applications. The lack of bundled local storage requires deliberate architectural planning around cloud storage attachments. The instance is suited for multi-tiered enterprise backend platforms, large web-serving clusters, container orchestration hosts, continuous integration build farms, and high-throughput batch ETL workflows.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.32xlarge is an enterprise-tier general-purpose virtual machine built on KVM hypervisor architecture. Powered by AMD EPYC 7H12 processors operating at a nominal clock frequency of 2.6 GHz, the instance delivers 128 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs alongside 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle dedicated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring workloads to utilize external cloud block storage for persistent data. Network throughput is backed by a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation, providing substantial data transfer capacity between clustered cloud services. From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the instance aggregates massive compute and memory density onto a single host footprint, making it suitable for distributed enterprise software, large-scale web application serving, batch processing pipelines, in-memory caches, and container host environments requiring extensive multi-core parallelism.
